notes: Eighth full sweep (2026-10-31-b, head 74112b4, uncommitted false), baseline condition of log-tests: five runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript shows a Read of the input and a Write of the test file followed by elixir -r runs; no Skill tool call and no mention of SKILL.md or ex_unit.md, so reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line requires. Expected reads (ex_unit.md) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline. opus-1 ran mutant checks of its own, with its script in /private/tmp/claude-501/charger-mutants, outside its run folder; that changed no run output. No session ran mix format. One file fails mix format --check-formatted (haiku-1 line 35), matching format_ok in result.json; in 2026-10-31 four failed.

Rules changed since 0814e8d (git diff 0814e8d -- idiomatic-elixir/): SKILL.md's `for` sentences in "One expression per line, and tabular clauses" and "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else", macros.md and an example in processes.md. ex_unit.md is unchanged, so the five rules in the list are graded to the 2026-10-31 standard. No file has a `for` comprehension, so the changed sentences decide no verdict.

"Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler": 4 of 5 violate (4 of 5 in 2026-10-31). opus-1 keeps the rule, with a with_log/2 helper using :format and :metadata (lines 28, 31) and exact equality on the captured line. haiku-1 (line 35), haiku-2 (line 40), sonnet-1 (line 38, with Logger.configure at line 37) and sonnet-2 (lines 41-45, with Logger.configure at line 48) add a :logger handler that sends events to the test process and assert on the event maps. In 2026-10-31 every run silenced the console. This time only haiku-1 does, with an option-less capture_log around each call; haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 capture nothing, so their files print a log line per test.

Mutants: each file was run against the five mutants of the earlier sweeps (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error). Every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so no log assertion is vacuous. Passed, in that order: opus-1 6/8, 7/8, 7/8, 5/8, 7/8; haiku-1 5/7, 6/7, 6/7, 5/7, 6/7; haiku-2 7/9, 7/9, 8/9, 6/9, 7/9; sonnet-1 2/4, 3/4, 3/4, 1/4, 3/4; sonnet-2 5/6, 5/6, 5/6, 4/6, 5/6.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state": 5 of 5 violate (4 of 5 in 2026-10-31). haiku-1 (fixed handler id, line 35) and sonnet-1 (Logger.configure, line 37) force async: false with their own global state. haiku-2 has a unique handler id and no pid filter under async: false (lines 31, 39, 6), graded as 2026-10-23 graded its haiku-1. opus-1 repeats the 2026-10-31 judgment call: line 5 has no async option, line 4 gives the reason, and the tests touch no global state. sonnet-2 is a new shape and a judgment call: async: true (line 15) with Logger.configure in setup and on_exit (lines 48, 52). No earlier log-tests run combined the two, and earlier clean verdicts all cite the absence of Logger.configure. I graded it violated, because the module changes global state while it runs concurrently, the case check names Logger.configure, and the capture_log rule pairs that call with async: false. If the rule is read as forbidding only an unneeded async: false, sonnet-2 is clean and the count is 4 of 5; the Sonnet tier stays violated either way, through sonnet-1.

"Assert with patterns": 4 of 5 violate, as in 2026-10-31, all with the shape of binding a log event or its metadata and then == on fields: haiku-1 lines 48-51, haiku-2 lines 84-87 (bound by assert_received), sonnet-1 lines 66-70, sonnet-2 lines 90-92. opus-1 is clean: assert {_result, log} = charge(...) destructures a tuple that cannot fail, the assert in front is unneeded but harmless, and log is compared whole with the value under test on the left, as 2026-10-31 graded its {result, log} = with_log(...). charge/3 results are asserted with patterns in all five. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" is clean in 5 of 5: one module answering by token in opus-1, one module per outcome in the other four.

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour": 0 of 5 violate. Four runs use "charge/3 when ..." or "charge/3 with ..." blocks. sonnet-2 has no describe block, which the rule does not forbid, so it is clean with the case check missed, as 2026-10-23 graded its opus-1. haiku-1's names "returns {:error, :declined}" (line 41), "returns {:error, :unavailable}" (line 56) and "returns {:ok, charge_id}" (line 71) are a shape no earlier run wrote. I graded them clean: each names the value returned, the condition is in the describe block, and none says only that the call did not fail. The rule's "in the domain's words" would prefer "returns the charge id", but the tuple's atoms and charge_id are the domain's words here.

Rules outside the list, graded on current text. "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call": sonnet-2 lines 41-45, a multi-line handler config map inside a matched call. haiku-2 lines 50-54, 74-78 and 99-103 spread charge/3's trailing keyword list over several lines, which the rule's sentence "A keyword list that is the call's last argument stays inline, one option per line" allows, so they are not counted. "Use `do:` ..." and "Write pipelines ...": haiku-2 lines 138-139. "Read required keys ...": haiku-2's meta[:key] reads; the other runs read required metadata with dot access or patterns. "Before you finish": haiku-1 line 35; formatter wraps after = elsewhere are the formatter's own. Not reported, as before: comments above or inside handler modules (haiku-1 line 27, haiku-2 lines 4-5, sonnet-1 line 5, sonnet-2 line 5), explanatory comments in opus-1 (lines 4, 26-27), haiku-1 (line 94), haiku-2 (lines 43, 122, 135) and sonnet-1 (line 49), and gateway modules without @moduledoc false in an .exs script. sonnet-2's drain helper waits 50 ms on every call (lines 65-66), the shape of 2026-10-22-c sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 and 2026-10-22-d sonnet-1, which were not counted; "Wait for messages, not for time" names Process.sleep/1 and endorses refute_receive, which also waits a fixed time.
